title: Amazon makes its AI-powered Alexa+ free on Fire TV, no Prime required
slides: Can Alexa+ finally make Fire TV worth it?
It's free, no Prime membership required.
But previous Alexa promises left users skeptical.
Now TV searches, recommendations, and dialogue become conversational.
Test it tonight: ask your Fire TV a complex question.
thread_text:
1. The free upgrade

Alexa+ lands on Fire TV at no extra cost, and it doesn't need a Prime subscription to work.

2. Trust issues

Past Alexa promises fell flat, so users are right to doubt whether the new conversational search will actually deliver.

3. Talk to your TV

Now you can ask complex questions and get natural, spoken answers instead of scrolling through menus or typing.

4. The real test

Conversational recommendations might change how you find shows, but only if the AI understands what you actually mean.

5. Try it tonight

Ask your Fire TV: "What's a good sci-fi movie from the 90s with a twist ending?" See what it says.

instagram.caption:
Alexa+ is now free on Fire TV, and you don't need a Prime membership to get it.  

The catch? Amazon has burned you before with Alexa promises that flopped, so skepticism is fair. This time, the pitch is conversational search: ask your TV a complex question and get a spoken answer instead of scrolling menus.  

For creators and publishers, this shifts how your content gets discovered—if the AI recommends it, you're on the watchlist. If it doesn't, you're invisible.  

Tonight, ask your Fire TV: “What’s a good 90s sci-fi with a twist ending?” Does it get you, or does it stall? 🤔📺🧠
